knot-field.look: The vol view proves it. Tube mode draws a literal, clean trefoil, cinquefoil, 8_19 or a 3-ring link of constant radius floating in empty space (the raw |f| tube from the idea pinches badly, the Gauss-Newton distance fixes it exactly). Fibre bundle mode (a new mode found here: Worley on the f plane, wires of uniform radius) looks like hundreds of magnetic field lines or combed hair wrapped round a 3- or 5-lobed core and is the best image of the family. Hopf + Worley gives a whirl of tapered horns converging on a centre. The 2D claim in the idea was wrong for Hopf: slices are a whirlpool of scales, concentric at z=0 and a pinwheel at z=1.2. Flaws seen: it is one centred object that fades to a constant far from the origin; fold makes it stationary but the 2D sheet is then an obvious mirrored carpet of whirlpools; Pages (Seifert sheets) are a smooth blob with thin sheets and render striations; Milnor with a source looks like a generic blobby warp with big cut faces; per-cell scatter reads as macaroni once knots overlap, and the own-cell tumbleweed is a regular grid of fuzzy balls with solid-looking cores.
knot-field.dims: 3D is the real form, using a real Eval3. 2D is a slice at z0: Hopf modes look good; tube and bundle reduce to dots and dashes, which is inherent. 4D was tested only as a parameter: w rotates S3 through the pole, 2 pi periodic by construction, and the knot flows out of the frame and returns (frames rendered at w=0.6, 1.57, 2.6). Clifford tiling: Hopf is a function of a-b only by derivation, 1D stripes, not rendered; Milnor rendered once as a diagonal woven moire, modest look, and tiling was not separately checked.
knot-field.range: tube and bundle clamp to [-1,1] by construction. Hopf+Perlin measured -0.886..0.919 with gain 1.4 over 8 seeds. Hopf+Worley -1..0.95.
knot-field.artifacts: Vol renders need finer marching for thin wires: k=8, tube=0.02 at default steps shows dotted wires; this looks like a march miss, though that was not isolated from the bundle continuity issue. Thin tubes will alias in real use.
knot-field.node_shape: KnotField: Mode enum (HopfSource, KnotTube, FibreBundle), Source (HopfSource only, evaluated at k*h), Scale, Source Scale k, P, Q (int), Tube Radius (hybrid), Phase w (hybrid, S3 rotation, the 4D axis), Fold (float, 0 = off), Seed, Feature Scale. Drop Pages, Milnor-with-source and per-cell scatter.
knot-field.port_notes: Polynomials plus Reciprocal and square root; P,Q are constant-count complex multiply loops. Scalar ns/sample (perlin2 about 51): tube 206 (4.00x), Hopf+Perlin3 300 (5.85x), Hopf+Worley3 318 (6.25x), bundle 299 (5.66x); 3x3x3 scatter of trefoils 1759 (35x, before the floor fix). The prototype calls sin/cos for phase per sample, so these overstate a port. Hopf uniform radius needs no Jacobian: across fibres |dh| = 4 D |dX| with D = 1/(r^2+1). Milnor distance needs the 2x3 Jacobian. Use a scale-invariant floor det + 1e-3*(A+C)^2: an absolute floor made the far field read as solid, measured and fixed. Search bundle features in the Gauss-Newton metric. check: tube c0ratio 8.11; Hopf+Worley 7.99; bundle c0ratio 1.11 to 1.83 with max slope 793 to 1025, so thin bundle wires are not cleanly continuous at the probe scale. The likely cause is a near-degenerate J, unconfirmed and unresolved. Seed sensitivity is 0 for pure tube, which has no randomness. Far coords are constant as designed unless Fold is on.

critic.notes: The vol view decides and it does prove the look: the fibre bundle is the best image in the family, the trefoil and cinquefoil tubes are clean and constant-radius, and seed 7 bundle looks like seed 0 (not cherry-picked). Re-measured: bundle scalar 244 ns (4.8x perlin2), check c0ratio 1.53 with max slope 514 (the wire discontinuity is real), far coords -1 std 0; tube check with hero params is -1 everywhere (c0ratio 0.00, std 0): the field is a constant except at one spot. AVX2 sketch reproduced: tube 1.8 ns, Hopf lift 0.4 ns. The decisive flaw for a noise library: it is one centred object. vol at window 10 shows a small pom-pom in an empty cube; the 2D whirl at window 16 is one spiral whose scales grow to screen size away from the centre (sheet axis 9.3). Fold makes a mirrored carpet, scatter and tumbleweed were rightly dropped. Nothing in existing nodes produces a torus knot or Hopf whirl, but a technical artist wanting a knot would model one; the realistic use is a demo scene or a one-off hero object. Variants P=2,Q=2 (Hopf link bundle) and P=5,Q=2 render well, so the mode generalises. Hopf+Worley with uni=1 gives uniform tapered horns, still with large cut faces.
critic.improved: No better hero image. Added variety renders at P=2,Q=2 and P=5,Q=2, the window-10 evidence render and the seed-3 window-16 whirl sheet; uni=1 whirl was not an improvement.

tournament.notes: Best image in the family, but a single centred object that is a constant everywhere else; check with hero params is -1 everywhere. Bundle discontinuity confirmed (c0ratio 1.53, max slope 514). Scalar 244 ns bundle (4.8x perlin2); AVX2 sketch tube 1.8 ns, Hopf lift 0.4 ns reproduced. Seed 7 bundle matches seed 0. A demo object, not noise; a technical artist would model a knot rather than evaluate a field for it.
tournament.est_avx2_ns: AVX2 sketch, MEASURED for cost only: tube P=3,Q=2 with Gauss-Newton distance 1.7 ns; Hopf lift without source 0.4 ns. Calibration in the same sketch: Perlin 0.7 ns and cellular 3D 8.7 ns against the handbook's 1.1 and 12. ESTIMATE for a real node at about 1.4x: tube about 2.4 ns in 2D/3D/4D with no lattice; Hopf lift about 0.6 ns plus the source. Bundle about 7 ns is an ESTIMATE only, not benched.

artist-terrain.note: Fibre-bundle vol is one of the best pictures in the whole set and totally useless for terrain: one centred object, constant elsewhere. Demo.

artist-material.note: Spectacular hairball, but one centred object and -1 everywhere else. A demo.

voxel-engineer.note: Stunning object, constant -1 elsewhere. Not noise.

maintainer.note: Fibre bundle vol is the most beautiful image in the tournament and the trefoil tube is clean; but it is one centred object and -1 everywhere else. Not a noise node. Front-page picture, nothing more.

graphics-researcher.note: The fibre bundle volume is among the best images of the tournament and the Hopf whirl is lovely, but it is one centred object that is -1 everywhere else; a demo, not noise.

creative.note: The fibre bundle and the whirl of scales are astonishing images. It is a single centred object, not a field.

master.one_liner: Stereographic lift of 3D space to S3, then Hopf or Milnor map to a low-dimensional source: fields whose level sets are linked rings or literal torus knots.
master.look: 3D volumes with impossible structure: interlocked ring clouds, magnetic-field-like plasma, trefoil caves and lattice of chained cells. In 2D slices it looks only like smooth low-frequency warp and is dull (prototype confirmed this), so this is a 3D or volumetric node. Good for hero caves, magic plasma, strange attractor clouds. Prototyped 2D slice only: mode=11.
master.algorithm: X = p*s, r2 = |X|^2, n = (2X, r2-1)/(r2+1) on S3, with u = n0+i*n1, v = n2+i*n3. Hopf mode: h = (2 Re(u conj v), 2 Im(u conj v), |u|^2-|v|^2) on S2, output S3(k*h): constant along linked Villarceau circles, so every isosurface is a linked set of tori. Milnor mode with integers (P,Q): f = u^P + v^Q in C, output S2(k Re f, k Im f), or Tube: 1-2*smoothstep(0,Tube,|f|). The zero set of u^2+v^3 on S3 is a trefoil, so Tube carves a literal knotted tube in a volume. Polys only, no atan. For a stationary field pre-apply pmm fold (tri on each axis), giving a lattice of knots with continuous joins.
master.why_new: Topology cannot be made by warping noise, as warps are homeomorphisms of the plain source and cannot generate linking or knots on demand. Very cheap, with no lattice.
master.simd_plan: About 15 multiplies and 1 divide, under 1 ns (estimate), plus a 3D (Hopf) or 2D (Milnor) source. P,Q small ints with constant multiply loops. Input 2D: slice at constant z. Input 4D: skip stereographic, normalise p onto S3 directly (bounded and elegant, and GenTileable torus input lands exactly on a Clifford torus of S3, worth testing).
master.continuity: C-infinity as rational functions, except for optional fold creases. Field tends to constant at infinity since all far points map near the pole.
master.params: Mode enum (Hopf, Milnor, Tube), Scale s, P, Q, Source Scale k, Tube Radius, Lattice Fold flag, Source.
master.risks: Niche and hero-object unless lattice folded. Isosurface knot look has not been rendered in 3D, only derived, so it needs a raymarch or marching-cube look test before any node work. Knot tube thickness varies strongly with distance from origin since stereographic is non-uniform.
master.cost_note: About 15 multiplies and 1 divide, under 1 ns (estimate), plus a 3D (Hopf) or 2D (Milnor) source.

queue.name: KnotField
queue.reason: Wild card. Hopf and Milnor lifts give linked and knotted isosurfaces for ~15 mults. Top distinct score, but never rendered, so the prototype must prove the 3D look.

coral-noise.look: Reef layout (roots on a plane, y up, seabed floor) gives real 3D branching objects from a pointwise function: staghorn coral, sea fan, finger coral, and with thinner params a bare winter forest on a snowy plain. Growth along age works as promised and is the best part: stumps, trunks, branches appearing where the parent has passed the attach point, twigs, then thickening. The idea's own 3D lattice is the weak form: floating sticks and sparse needles in a volume. 2D is scattered branching twigs or crack-like dendrites that also grow; useful as a mask, plain as an image. Flaws seen: lattice rows are faintly visible at jit 0.5, thin twigs alias to dots, the 2D relief is ragged mesas, the inverted cave test showed almost nothing in the vol view, and it is very expensive.
coral-noise.dims: 2D and 3D measured and rendered. Age is a parameter in the prototype; the 4D form (w = age) is the same code with per-lane age and is included in the AVX2 sketch. Age continuity was measured, but no 4D view or tiling test exists.
coral-noise.range: Solid output clamps to [-1,1]; measured -1 to 0.637 for staghorn in 2D slices, 3D reaches 1.0 inside the floor. out=1 is a clamped scaled SDF.
coral-noise.artifacts: Thin twigs drop to dotted pixels at default march steps (renderer) and alias at low sample rates (real). Reef trees are cut by the render cube, which shows as orange slivers.
coral-noise.node_shape: CoralNoise: Layout enum (Reef = roots on plane, 3x3; Lattice = 3x3x3), Levels (int), Children (int), BranchLength, LengthRatio, Radius, RadiusRatio, Taper, Spread, UpBias (negative = roots), AttachMin, Jitter, Density, Age (hybrid; w in 4D), AgeJitter, Smooth, Template Count (0 = per segment hash), Output enum (Solid, SDF), optional floor height or leave the floor to a graph Min.
coral-noise.port_notes: The proto outputs a clamped falloff band, which only has to be exact near the surface, so trees can reach past the idea's 0.9 extent. Seam test against one extra ring of cells: staghorn 0 on 3 slices; forest with jit 0.5, L0 0.8, spread 0.8 0 on 3 slices at seed 7; jit 0.9, dens 0.7 max 0.018; the larger L0 0.9, jit 0.8 trees reached a max error of 1.07 on 1 slice in 3 with mean 0.000, so Jitter and BranchLength must be limited. Reef has no y window, so tree height is free. Smooth min only inside a tree, whose order is fixed; trees are hard-min'd, so crossing a cell never changes the order. Template trick: build K trees at set-param time; a cell then needs only hash, root, table rotation about y and scale, and capsule constants are splats. A forest with 1 template looked much the same as unique trees at the wide view and measured 1.75x to 1.79x faster. Scalar ns/sample (perlin2 about 50): forest 3212 (63x), staghorn 7221 (138x), 2D twig 3640 (73x), inflated by sin/cos per segment.

critic.params: staghorn: levels=4,kids=2,L0=0.35,lr=0.84,r=0.075,rr=0.92,taper=0.97,spread=1.05,up=1.4,sk=0.05,tmin=0.3,jit=0.6,y0=0.75,cell=0.7,fk=0.05,age=1.5 (vol --window 2.5 --steps 320); with ageJit=0.9,jit=0.9,dens=0.8 for size variety. forest: levels=2,kids=3,L0=0.8,lr=0.62,r=0.09,spread=0.8,sk=0.05,jit=0.5,y0=0.75 (vol --window 8)
critic.notes: Growth in the extra dimension is real: the strips show stumps, trunks, branches, twigs, thickening, and nothing pops; this is the showpiece and it holds. Seed 7 staghorn and forest match the seed 0 look. Re-measured: forest scalar 3180 ns (64x perlin2), staghorn 7155 ns (121x), check c0ratio 8.0, far coords fine, no NaNs. AVX2 sketch reproduced: 36 capsules 55 ns, 117 capsules 157 ns unique / 88 ns template, 279 capsules 358 / 203 ns, 3D lattice 189 capsules 271 ns; the idea's 45 ns was 6x too low as the prototyper said. Flaws seen: trees are capsule unions with identical size per cell, so the 2D wide view is a lattice of equal glyphs (sheet axis 8.06) and the reef reads as one tree per cell; the one-template forest repeats visibly at window 4 (same silhouette rotated), which the prototyper did not assess; the scalar prototype shows no template speed-up (3189 vs 3180 ns), the 1.79x is only in the sketch; thin twigs dot at default march steps; seam safety depends on limiting Jitter and BranchLength. No existing node or graph can produce branching objects, so unique is high, but at 90 to 360 ns per sample in AVX2 and a 130-segment fixed-count loop this is a bake or hero node, not a building block. Would a technical artist reach for it: for voxel coral, dead trees or roots, yes occasionally; the result still needs sculpt-level control they will not get from 15 scalar knobs.
critic.improved: ageJit=0.9,jit=0.9,dens=0.8 on the staghorn gives mixed tree sizes and breaks the one-per-cell sameness a little; modest gain. Added a render as evidence of template repetition.

tournament.notes: Growth is the showpiece and it holds: strips show stumps to trunks to branches to twigs to thickening with nothing popping. Seed 7 matches seed 0. Scalar 3180 ns forest (64x perlin2), 7155 ns staghorn (121x); check c0ratio 8.0, no NaNs. AVX2 sketch reproduced: 55 to 358 ns unique, 88 to 203 ns template, 3D lattice 271 ns. Flaws: capsule-union silhouettes, equal-size tree per cell (2D wide view is a glyph lattice, axis 8.06), one-template forest repeats visibly close up, no template speed-up in the scalar proto, thin twigs dot at default march steps, seam safety needs Jitter and BranchLength limits. Nothing existing makes branching objects, but at this cost and code size it is a bake or hero node.
tournament.est_avx2_ns: AVX2 sketch, MEASURED for cost only (output not compared with the scalar prototype). Reef or 2D, 9 cells: L1 K3 36 capsules 55 ns; L2 K3 117 capsules 160 ns unique, 90 ns template; L4 K2 279 capsules 367 ns unique, 209 ns template. 3D lattice L2 K2 189 capsules 278 ns. Calibration in the same sketch: Perlin 0.7 ns and cellular 3D 8.7 ns against the handbook's 1.1 and 12. ESTIMATE for a real node at about 1.4x: reef forest 125 ns template or 225 ns unique; 2D about the same as reef at equal capsule count; 4D about the same as the 3D form, since w is only age. The idea's 45 ns for 189 capsules was about 6x too low.

artist-terrain.note: Reef layout gives staghorn, sea fan, winter forest with continuous growth; 64-121x Perlin, capsule silhouettes, glyph lattice in 2D. Hero bake only.

master.one_liner: Exact SDF to a lattice of hierarchically branching capsules (root segment per cell, M children per segment, L levels) where w is growth age: coral, bare trees, roots, neurons, lightning and needle crystals that grow in place.
master.look: 3D iso at 0: fields of small branching corals or bare shrubs rising from seed points; UpBias < 0 gives root systems; Spread small, M=1, Levels 2 with per-level kinks gives lightning/Lichtenberg bolts; Levels=0 gives random oriented needles (acicular crystals, hoarfrost, hay). As w increases, trunks extend, then branches sprout where the trunk has reached their attach point, then twigs: a genuine growth animation. 2D slice: short dashes, dots and Y-shapes; a 2D-native Gen gives bare-tree silhouettes / cracks that branch.
master.algorithm:
Window 3x3x3 (3x3 2D). Per cell k: h = Hash(k); a0 = k + 0.5 + 0.2*rnd3(h); u0 = normalize(rndDir3(h>>8) + UpBias*(0,1,0)); L0 = BranchLength (<= 0.35).
Fixed-count enumeration of the branch tree (Levels in 0..2, Children M in 1..3, count sum M^l per cell): child j of segment (a, u, L, birth): hj = Hash(h, j, level); attach t_j in [0.4,1] from hj; aj = a + t_j*L*u; uj = normalize(u + Spread*rndDir3(hj)); Lj = L*0.6; birth_j = birth + t_j*L/Speed.
Growth (age A = w in 4D, or Age hybrid in 2D/3D; A = infinity if unused): len = Clamp((A - birth)*Speed, 0, L); rad = Radius*0.6^level * Min(1, len/(0.1 L)) (radius grows in over the first 10 percent of life so a segment never pops); segment b = a + len*u.
d = capsuleDistance(p, a, b) - rad; sdf = Min over all segments of all 27 cells (unborn segments have len=0 and rad=0, contributing a point of radius 0: mask them to BIG with Select(A > birth, d, BIG)).
Extent from cell centre <= 0.2 + 0.35 + 0.21 + 0.126 < 0.9, so cells two away stay >= 0.6 from the sample: exact for Radius < 0.6. Output: Signed SDF (scaled) or Solid = Clamp(1 - sdf/Radius).
master.why_new: The graph cannot make branching 1D structures at all. Exact Lipschitz-1 SDF means offsets, shells and sphere tracing work; growth as a parameter is free; needle noise alone is a new look.
master.simd_plan: Cellular.inl window loop with an inner fixed-count tree loop; every segment is a capsule distance (~20 ops) plus hash/normalize per segment (normalize = InvSqrt). Levels=1,M=3: 4 segments/cell x 27 = 108 capsules ~ 2x CellularDistance 3D (25 ns); Levels=2,M=2: 7/cell = 189 capsules ~ 3.5x (45 ns); 2D ~ 2x CellularDistance 2D. 4D = 3D lattice with w as age (tiles correctly since continuous in w). A true 4D lattice is not recommended.
master.continuity: C0 (min of exact capsule SDFs, |grad| <= 1); continuous in w thanks to the radius grow-in.
master.params: BranchLength, Radius (hybrid), Children (int 1-3), Levels (int 0-2), Spread, UpBias, Speed, Age (hybrid, 2D/3D), Feature Scale, Seed, Output enum.
master.risks: Cost scales with 27 x segments; the 'children only of the 2-3 nearest roots' shortcut would halve it but introduces seams where the nearest root switches, so it should be an explicit quality option at most. Lattice regularity of one tree per cell needs jitter plus a Density mask (hybrid) to kill some roots for natural clumping.
master.cost_note: Levels=1,M=3: 4 segments/cell x 27 = 108 capsules ~ 2x CellularDistance 3D (25 ns); Levels=2,M=2: 7/cell = 189 capsules ~ 3.5x (45 ns); 2D ~ 2x CellularDistance 2D.

queue.name: CoralNoise
queue.reason: Wild card. Exact SDF to a growing branching capsule forest, with growth in w as the showpiece. 100-190 capsules per sample rules out regular use, but the look may justify a hero node.

newton-basins.look: Flat patches meeting along curved lobed borders, with occasional zones of interleaved tongues and palm-like fronds, some with smooth banded shading. Side by side with a warped CellularValue graph the difference is plain: the graph gives flat cells with wiggly borders and no fronds. Fronds cover only part of a view, and from far away (window 16) it reads as an ordinary mosaic. Relief is stepped mesas with sheer cliffs. RootDist gives smooth wells between ornate walls. In 3D the XZ slice is as ornate as 2D and the vol view is shattered rubble with speckle, so 3D works but is less attractive than 2D. Flaws seen: hard jumps everywhere by design, small aliased wedges remain, and static patches appear at high N or large maxstep.
newton-basins.dims: 2D and 3D (3 noises, Cramer solve) rendered and checked. 4D not prototyped, it needs a cofactor solve, so tiling is untested.
newton-basins.range: Root value clamps to [-1,1], measured -1 to 1 over 8 seeds. RootDist has no analytic range and is clamped.
newton-basins.artifacts: Hard edges and tiny wedges will alias at low sample rates, so expect to need supersampling or a filter (not tested). Without offsets the wide view shows a clear lattice. High N or maxstep over about 0.7 fills zones with TV static.
newton-basins.node_shape: NewtonBasins: Iterations (int, default 4), MaxStep (hybrid, default 0.35), DetFloor (default 0.5, a cheap replacement for Levenberg damping), ValueSource (optional GeneratorSource sampled at q, default an internal noise), Output enum (RootValue, RootDistance, SoftCount), Seed, Feature Scale.
newton-basins.port_notes: Critical bug to avoid: Perlin vanishes on the integer lattice, so two seeded Perlins share a root at every lattice point and the basins form a square grid. The earlier dyn_lens code has no offsets, so the look it was judged on would have had this flaw. Offset each noise by a fixed non-integer vector: FFT axis ratio dropped from 50.92 to 7.66 at equal settings and the wide view lost the grid. A sign-preserving det floor of 0.5 keeps fronds at no added cost; the Levenberg form needs a larger solve in 3D. N=3 to 5 looks at least as good as N=12 with less static. Scalar ns/sample (perlin2 about 50): N=4 789 (15.75x), N=6 1003 (19.87x). check: c0ratio 1.00 and max slope 2000 per unit, real jumps by design; 3D z-continuity max 1.62 for dz=1e-3; seed sensitivity 0.606; far coords std 0.417; no NaNs.

critic.params: N=4,maxstep=0.35,dfloor=0.5 (--window 5); out=5 for the relief (unconverged points fade to grey)
critic.notes: Re-measured: scalar 800 ns (16x perlin2), AVX2 sketch N=4 16.9 ns reproduced, c0ratio 1.00 by design, 3D z-continuity max 1.62. The hero sheet is a favourable seed: at seed 3 the fronds shrink to a few small zones and most of the frame is a plain flat mosaic; at seed 11 window 16 it is a speckled mosaic, and axis stays 14 to 19 across my sheets, so a mild lattice alignment survives the offsets. I rendered the real existing-node graph with fnlab (DomainWarpFractalProgressive over CellularValue): it gives flat patches with marbled borders and no fronds, so the prototyper is right that the lace cannot be had from a graph, but the lace covers a minority of the area and the rest is what the graph already does. The relief with out=5 is a cleaner mesa terrain than the default relief (static greys out), yet Terrace on a warped noise gives comparable plateaus. oct=2 adds lace everywhere but it is mostly static. 3D is rubble. Hard jumps, wedge aliasing and static make it hard to use in production. The stained-glass and agate variants are lattice-locked or 34x perlin.
critic.improved: out=5 relief is cleaner. oct=2 made it noisier, not better. Added a render as the honest seeds, and the fnlab comparison.

tournament.notes: Scalar 800 ns (16x perlin2); AVX2 sketch N=4 16.9 ns reproduced; c0ratio 1.00 by design; 3D z-continuity max 1.62. Hero sheet is a favourable seed: seed 3 has fronds in a few small zones only, seed 11 at window 16 is a speckled mosaic, axis 14 to 19 so mild lattice alignment survives the offsets. Real existing graph (DomainWarpFractalProgressive over CellularValue in fnlab) gives flat patches with marbled borders and no fronds; the fronds are genuinely new but cover a minority of the area, the rest is the graph. Hard jumps, wedge aliasing, static and a rubble 3D. Stained glass is lattice-locked, agate cells cost 34x perlin.
tournament.est_avx2_ns: AVX2 sketch, MEASURED for cost only, 2D: N=3 12.9, N=4 16.9, N=6 25.1, N=8 33.2 ns. Calibration in the same sketch: Perlin 0.7 ns and cellular 3D 8.7 ns against the handbook's 1.1 and 12. ESTIMATE for a real node at about 1.4x: 2D N=4 about 24 ns. 3D N=4 about 45 ns and 4D N=4 about 110 ns, both ESTIMATES from gradient counts, not benched.

artist-terrain.note: Fronds only in a few zones on the hero seed; seed 11 w16 is a speckled mosaic; c0 1, 3D z-jumps 1.62, 17 ns at N=4.

artist-material.note: The hero is a favourable seed. Other seeds are a speckled mosaic, and the relief is broken pillars.

master.one_liner: Damped Newton on a pair (or D-tuple) of noises, coloured by the root reached: smooth patches meeting along genuinely fractal fern-like and scalloped borders with zero octaves.
master.look:
Verified at zoom. Large flat patches, with parts of the borders in Julia-style lobes, scallops and fern fronds, and occasional chaotic wedges of tiny detail near curves where det J=0. Boundary detail is self-similar with no octaves. Good for alien terrain masks, stained-glass or lichen, mineral inclusions, fantasy map provinces with ornate coasts.
[NewtonBasin, dynamics-iteration] A mosaic of basins, each a smooth region around one root, separated by boundaries that near every basin triple point fragment into ever-finer interleaved tongues (Wada-like Newton fractal lace) when Damping is small; Residual draws those boundaries as bright circuit-like filaments on a black field; SoftCount shades each basin with concentric convergence bands. Raising Damping continuously morphs it into a soft organic cell map similar to FlowWatershed's catchments. Textures: cracked lacquer, circuit traces, lichen, frost ferns; masks for 'where things break'.
master.algorithm:
F(q)=(n1(q),n2(q)). Repeat N (6..8): evaluate n1,n2 and gradients; det=ax*by-ay*bx with sign-preserving floor |det|>=1e-3; s=(by*n1-ay*n2, -bx*n1+ax*n2)/det; scale s to |s|<=MaxStep (about 0.35); q-=s. Output a value noise or ColorSource sampled at q. In 3D use 3 noises with a 3x3 Cramer solve; 4D uses 4 noises with a cofactor solve. Prototype: dyn_lens mode=5,N=8,maxstep=0.35; zoom with sheet --window 3.

[NewtonBasin, dynamics-iteration] F(p) = (f_1(p), ..., f_d(p)) d internal gradient noises; roots are isolated points (about one per few cells). J = [d f_i / d x_j].
  q = p; count = 0
  for k in 0..N-1:
      f = F(q); J = Jac(q)
      step = (J^T J + lambda I)^-1 J^T f          // Levenberg-Marquardt; lambda=0 is pure Newton (J^-1 f). 2x2/3x3 closed form, 4x4 cofactors
      step *= min(1, maxStep / (|step| + 1e-9))   // clamp jump length, branch-free
      q = q - step
      count += smoothstep(eps2, eps1, |F(q)|)     // fractional 'already converged' count
  Output enum:
    RootId   : rnd11(hash(floor(q*CellScale)))  or Source B(q)
    Residual : |F(q)| remapped
    SoftCount: count / N

master.why_new: Fractal detail here comes from dynamics, not added frequency, so it only appears at borders, while interiors stay perfectly flat. Thresholded FBm and warped Cellular cannot have flat interiors with lobed fractal coasts.
master.simd_plan: 2N gradients in 2D (about 14 gradients, about 20 ns with analytic Perlin). 3D 3N gradients (about 60 ns). 4D 4N gradients (about 190 ns) plus a 4x4 solve, so offer 4D as expensive. Clamp with Min and Select only.
master.continuity: Discontinuous at basin borders (sign-preserving det floor, measured c0ratio 1.1). Interior C-infinity except where the step clamp is active.
master.params: Iterations, MaxStep (hybrid; lower gives less fractal more cell-like), Source pair frequency, Output enum (RootValue, RootDistance |q-p|), hybrid Value source.
master.risks:
Heavy high-frequency content in the wedges will alias at low sample rate; no analytic range on Distance output. 3D slices look less ornate than 2D. Two octaves become noisier, so keep the input simple.
[NewtonBasin, dynamics-iteration] Pure Newton can wander far (hence the clamp); fractal detail is unbounded so mipmapping/aliasing issues for rendering; needs the internal gradient-noise utility.
master.cost_note: 2N gradients in 2D (about 14 gradients, about 20 ns with analytic Perlin). 3D 3N gradients (about 60 ns).
master.variant_notes: Damping morphs from fractal lace to smooth cells. High-frequency wedges alias.
